answer: Plant a cedar: an identity only grows tall after seasons of verified work, so a sybil farm of fresh sprouts stays short. An ivory seal is carved once, by independent checkers, onto deeds that truly happened - it cannot be stamped in bulk. And a wharf forces every cargo of claims to dock in public, where anyone can inspect it before it is paid. A sybil can print a thousand names, but it cannot fake cedar-slow growth, ivory-hard proof, or a wharf in daylight - so the economy pays age and evidence, not volume.
